_about: Brand data choices read by scripts/import-brands.ts (v1.2 follow-up plan WP10, open question Q16).

Each decision has a proposed default. status is "PENDING FOUNDER" until the founder answers; then set status to "DECIDED", put the answer in chosen (copy proposed to accept it) and say who decided and where it is recorded in source (for example "founder, 2026-11-20, spec v1.2-phase5-7 (p)"). The generator refuses a DECIDED entry without source.

While a decision is PENDING the generator uses proposed, with one exception: a pending answer never releases a held row. behrouz_city and dominos_duplicates resolve conflict-tier rows, so they take effect only once DECIDED.
Rows with qa_severity error are never released by any decision (they change only when the brand publishes a corrected document).
Decisions marked 'recorded only' do not change any row; the generator copies them into the migration header and scripts/brands/out/manifest.json for the resolver half of WP10.
Promotion (npx tsx scripts/import-brands.ts --number NNN) refuses while any decision is PENDING FOUNDER or a brand with served rows has no sign-off.
After editing this file run: npx tsx scripts/import-brands.ts && npx tsx scripts/import-brands.ts --check

atwater_rule.question: Which Atwater tolerance gates a brand row? A row passes when |kcal - (4P + 4C + 9F)| is within pct% of kcal OR within kcal_slack kcal. kcal_slack 0 means a pure +/-pct% rule.
atwater_rule.why: This is REPORT.md's QA rule. Founder (n) says +/-15%, but a pure percentage fails near-zero items where the brand's own rounding dominates (Burger King Hot Espresso Small: 4 kcal printed, 5.1 from its macros). The 15 kcal slack only matters below 100 kcal; a pure 15% rule fails 30 more rows, almost all drinks, sachets and teas under 40 kcal.
atwater_rule.effect: Rows that fail are held (gate:atwater_mismatch). Rows without all of P, C and F cannot be checked; see macros_incomplete.

starbucks_guide.question: Starbucks India: which nutrition guide is the source of truth?
starbucks_guide.why: linked_2023 is the PDF starbucks.in links today (content dated 02-01-2023, file Jun 2026), and it is the only guide in _combined.csv. The Feb-2026 guide sits on Tata Starbucks' pre-production storage; we could not confirm the live site links it, and it disagrees on 194 of 529 item+size pairs. The linked guide's known errors (Short = Tall Cappuccino at 104 kcal) are already held by the size check.
starbucks_guide.effect: feb_2026 withholds all 976 current Starbucks rows (unserved, decision:starbucks_guide) until that guide is collected and QA'd into _combined.csv.

mcdonalds_default_region.question: McDonald's India has two franchisees with different numbers (17 of 26 shared item+size pairs differ). Which region serves when we do not know the user's region within India?
mcdonalds_default_region.why: The West & South booklet covers more items (134 vs 93), is 97% clean and prints a gram or ml weight on every row. North & East is newer (Dec 2025) but 27 of its rows have no weight and 14 are kcal-only.
mcdonalds_default_region.effect: Sets is_default_region on McDonald's rows. Both regions stay verified; the default region wins when both publish the item, and an item only one region publishes is still served from that region.

behrouz_city.question: Behrouz Biryani prints different values for the same item in different cities (50 conflict rows). Which city's values do we serve?
behrouz_city.why: Both cities' listings say 'Served with 1 Gulab Jamun & Mint Raita'. The Gurgaon/Delhi (IN-NCR) values include the gulab jamun's sugar (e.g. Lazeez Bhuna Murgh 948 kcal, 40 g sugar), so they match the box as sold; the Bengaluru values (733 kcal, 5 g sugar) look like the biryani alone. Under the whole-dish rule a named branded item is one food.
behrouz_city.effect: Once DECIDED: the chosen city's duplicate_conflict rows are released when that city has a single value; other cities' conflict rows stay held (decision:behrouz_city). 'none' keeps all 50 held. Also sets is_default_region for Behrouz rows. While PENDING nothing is released.

dominos_duplicates.question: Domino's charts some pizzas twice with different numbers (68 conflict rows, e.g. Double Cheese Margherita, Peppy Paneer). Which value do we keep?
dominos_duplicates.why: Nothing in the charts says which image is current, so we serve neither until a person compares them (or Domino's republishes). keep_higher_kcal is the cautious automatic pick if the founder prefers serving something.
dominos_duplicates.effect: Once DECIDED: keep_higher_kcal releases the higher-kcal row of each conflict group (ties stay held); keep_rows releases exactly the listed Domino's source rows (at most one per group). While PENDING nothing is released.

dominos_mni_34_40.question: Domino's regional chart images MNI-34..40 were not transcribed. Transcribe them?
dominos_mni_34_40.why: They are official charts like the other 40; the collectors stopped for time, not because of a data problem.
dominos_mni_34_40.effect: Recorded only: a collection task, not a generator rule. Those items have no rows until then.

default_size.question: When a user names a branded item without a size ('starbucks cappuccino', 'mcd fries'), which size do we serve? Per brand, an ordered list of size labels (normalized: lowercase, punctuation to spaces); within each item's listing (every size the brand prints, served or not), the first label that matches any row decides, and that row is the default only if it is the single match and is served. A label also matches a longer variant that starts with it ('personal' matches 'personal pan pizza').
options: any ordered label lists; fallback is always 'no default' (the resolver asks or falls through)
default_size.why: Each brand's standard serve: Starbucks Tall (the founder's own example), the 'Regular' size where a brand has one (McDonald's desserts and coffee, KFC and BK sides and drinks), Medium for McDonald's soft drinks (sold Small/Medium/Large), a Regular hand-tossed Domino's pizza (Domino's 'Regular serves 1'), a Personal Pizza Hut pizza, a 6-inch Subway. Note: McDonald's fries default to Regular (77 g); if meals are what users mean, Medium (109 g) is the alternative.
default_size.effect: Sets is_default_size. The pick is made over the brand's whole listing of the item (held and unserved sizes included; exact repeats count once, and so does a double-listed size once a DECIDED choice releases one copy) and sticks only if the picked row is served: a held Tall never hands the default to Grande, and an item whose other sizes are held is not 'listed once'. An item listed once is its own default when single_row_is_default is true. Groups where no label matches, a label matches two rows, or the picked row is not served get no default (the resolver asks or falls through).

per100_no_portion.question: La Pino'z (199 rows), Wow! Momo (8) and 2 Haldiram's rows publish values per 100 g with no portion weight. How are they served?
per100_no_portion.why: The per-100 g numbers are official; only the portion is missing. Serving them when the user states grams ('200 g la pinoz farmhouse pizza') uses no invented weight. Without a stated amount the item falls through to the normal path (the row still exists, so no web lookup). Note the tension with founder (n): 'every extracted row must ... have a serving size'; these rows have none, which is why keep_unserved is offered.
per100_no_portion.effect: stated_amount_only: served with amount_rule stated_only. keep_unserved: unserved (decision:per100_no_portion). Wow! Momo rows are also kcal-only, so macros_incomplete holds them either way.

macros_incomplete.question: 139 rows publish kcal without all of protein, carbs and fat (all 98 CCD rows, 14 McDonald's N&E menu rows, 10 Pizza Hut, all 8 Wow! Momo, 7 Blue Tokai, both Barista). They cannot pass the Atwater check (n) requires. Keep them in brand_items?
macros_incomplete.why: Kept, they are never served but they count as 'we hold this item', so WP11 does not spend a web lookup on a brand whose only official numbers are these. Omitted, WP11 may look them up (CCD publishes nothing better).
macros_incomplete.effect: keep_unserved: status unserved (decision:macros_incomplete). omit_from_table: the rows are left out of brand_items entirely (listed in the review list as omitted).

collector_suspect.question: 40 rows carry a collector note calling the printed numbers SUSPECT (REPORT.md caveat collector_noted: 'usable, but read the note first'). 36 are already held by an error-tier flag; 4 pass every gate: Theobroma Cappuccino 250 ml at 647.5 kcal ('implausible ... verify before use'), Amul IC Strawberry (every value identical to Amul IC Vanilla), Haldiram's Kaju Katli (sugar 0.25 g, sodium 615 mg) and Natural's Tropical Sundae (sugar 27 g > carbs 26 g, inside the 2% + 0.5 g tolerance). Serve those 4?
collector_suspect.why: Caveat rows are importable (README), but nothing in the import reads the note, and the per-brand sign-off samples only about 10 rows. The collectors traced these to the brand's own document and still called them suspect; a 647.5 kcal cappuccino served as verified is worse than falling through to the generic row. Withheld rows still count as 'we hold this item', so WP11 makes no web lookup for them.
collector_suspect.effect: withhold: the rows are unserved (decision:collector_suspect) and listed in the review list. serve: they are served like any other caveat row. Rows already held stay held either way.

brand_tier_precedence.question: When a brand word or a reviewed brand-only name is present ('mcd mcchicken', 'mcaloo tikki'), does the brand tier answer before the generic exact key?
brand_tier_precedence.why: REPORT.md order: user memory, then brand match, then verified key. The brand's own number beats a generic dish when the user named the brand. Without a brand word the generic key keeps answering ('masala chai' stays the home-made dish).
brand_tier_precedence.effect: Recorded only (resolver half of WP10). User-taught memory always stays above the brand tier.

mcchicken_live_key.question: 'mcchicken burger' is already a live food_items key. Repoint it to the official McDonald's row?
mcchicken_live_key.why: With the brand tier on, 'mcchicken' is a brand-only name and the brand row answers first, so the live key stops being reached for that phrase. Repointing would change real users' results before the flag is on.
mcchicken_live_key.effect: Recorded only (resolver half). brand_items never writes food_items.

ml_only_rows.question: Rows that publish millilitres only (1,161): convert with 1 g/ml?
ml_only_rows.why: Adversarial review #20 and scripts/data/brands/README.md: never invent a weight. They are stored and served per serving; serving_ml is kept and serving_g stays NULL.
ml_only_rows.effect: Fixed rule; the generator refuses any other value.
ml_only_rows.source: plan adversarial review #20; scripts/data/brands/README.md 'Rules for the import'

no_weight_rows.question: Per-serve rows with no published weight or volume (793, e.g. Domino's slices, Faasos wraps): serve them?
no_weight_rows.why: Adversarial review #20: serve per serving, never invent a weight.
no_weight_rows.effect: Fixed rule; the generator refuses any other value. serving_g and serving_ml stay NULL.

amul_source.question: Amul's numbers come from Dudhsagar Dairy (an Amul member union), not amul.com. Keep them?
amul_source.effect: Amul rows are treated like any other brand.

signoffs._about: Per-brand human sign-off: read about 10 random served rows against the cited page and record {"by": name, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "rows_checked": n, "note": "..."}. null = not signed. REPORT.md section 3.3.
